reason: The cbz/zip support is the one thing that makes me curious, so I'd install the portable zip and throw a few manga archives at it. But I'm not making a 0.4 one-person app my default, because if it dies in a year I've done the default-setting dance for nothing.
why_switch_or_not: I'd try it because it opens zip/cbz directly and is fast on next/back, which matters when I flip through a chapter. The listing doesn't say anything about a manga mode (double-page, right-to-left, fit-width), so I can't assume it reads comics well, and I'd have to tick the formats and set default by hand in Settings. A lot of the feature list (3D, RAW, PSD, editor) is stuff I'd never touch, so it doesn't pull me.
current_app_pros: Explorer thumbnails are already there, cost nothing and need no setup. Whatever app opens a file is fine for a single picture, and I don't have to think about it.
current_app_pains: Nothing much for single pictures. Reading cbz is the annoying part: I have to extract the archive or use some other tool, and the Explorer thumbnails don't help inside a zip.
objection: One developer, version 0.4. Will it still be maintained next year? I hate relearning things, so I won't commit to something that might get abandoned.
would_change_my_mind: A real cbz reading mode (page-by-page, RTL, remembers my place) that I check works with my own archives, plus a visible release history showing the dev keeps shipping updates.
